name: figL01_feature_distributions
title: LOGAN: feature distributions at fixed ORF length
caption: Distributions of amino-acid (AA) entropy, predicted 3Di entropy, 12-state entropy and 3Di–12-state mutual information (MI) for complete ORFs of 100–149 aa (a–d) and 200–299 aa (e–h) in 50,009 LOGAN metagenomes. Classes: complete Prodigal genes (Prodigal+), and Prodigal− ORFs that are antisense shadows, same-strand frameshift shadows or intergenic. Densities from exact histograms over all 89.99 billion ORFs (0.01-bit bins; no sampling); n per class in the legends.

name: figL02_models_beyond_length
title: LOGAN: what the structural features add beyond ORF length
caption: Average precision (a–d) and ROC AUC (e–h) of gradient-boosted classifiers separating complete Prodigal+ ORFs from complete Prodigal− ORFs, for four negative sets: all Prodigal−, antisense shadows, frameshift shadows and intergenic ORFs. Feature sets are nested on ORF length (dashed line: length alone). Five-fold cross-validation grouped by accession; metrics are population-weighted (sample weight = 1/sampling rate) over 9.5 million sampled complete ORFs from all 90 shards; error bars, ± SD across folds.

name: figL03_models_within_length
title: LOGAN: discrimination within ORF-length bins
caption: ROC AUC of out-of-fold model scores evaluated within ORF-length bins, for complete Prodigal+ ORFs against all complete Prodigal− ORFs (a) and against intergenic ORFs (b). Within a bin, length carries little information, so the length-only model falls towards 0.5 (dotted) from 75 aa upward while models including 3Di entropy remain high. Bins with fewer than 200 sampled positives or negatives are omitted. Same models and cross-validation as the beyond-length figure.

name: figL05_six_frame
title: LOGAN: six-frame inheritance, discrimination and Δ
caption: Six-frame experiment on 8.82 million complete Prodigal genes (1% deterministic sample, all 90 shards). (a) Spearman correlation between the value in Prodigal's selected frame and in each of the five alternative frames (same strand +1/+2, opposite strand a0–a2): length and AA entropy are partly shared between frames; 3Di entropy and MI are not. (b) Fraction of genes for which each feature ranks the selected frame first, in the top two or top three of six (5,722,417 genes with all five alternatives; ties counted fractionally; dotted lines, chance 1/6, 1/3, 1/2). (c–g) Distribution of Δ = selected-frame value − median of the five alternatives (central 99% shown); the fraction of genes with Δ > 0 is computed over all genes in the sample.

name: figL06_missed_gene_evidence
title: LOGAN: Foldseek evidence for missed-gene candidates and matched controls
caption: Structural (3Di+AA, solid) and sequence-only (AA, hatched) Foldseek evidence for 20,000 high-scoring intergenic ORFs ≥100 aa that Prodigal did not call (candidates, score ≥ the 0.90-precision threshold), and arms matched to them by nearest length and truncation: complete Prodigal genes (positive control), low-scoring intergenic ORFs, antisense and frameshift shadows, and the candidates with their 3Di strings shuffled (amino acids unchanged). (a) Hits with full-length mutual coverage (query and target coverage ≥0.8), the primary readout; (b) any hit at E ≤ 10⁻³. Databases: PDB100, AFDB/Swiss-Prot, CATH50, BFVD and AFDB50. The shuffled null has one full-length hit in 20,000.

name: figL08_contig_taxonomy
title: LOGAN: contig taxonomy and the eukaryotic test
caption: Kraken2 (2.17.2; PlusPFP 2023-06-05) classification of the 79,774 contigs carrying the Foldseek queries, re-streamed from LOGAN. (a) Contig class for each arm. (b) For candidates and complete Prodigal genes whose best full-length target is eukaryotic, the class of their contig: 69.8% of such candidates (n = 2,525) lie on eukaryotic contigs. PlusPFP contains a single animal genome (human), so animal contigs are reported as one group; 15.6% of contigs are unclassified.

name: figL09_prodigal_skip
title: LOGAN: why Prodigal did not call the candidates
caption: Prodigal 2.6.3 (-p meta) rerun on the query contigs with -s, which lists every potential gene and its scores; the rerun reproduces all original calls. For each query, the best-scoring potential gene ending at its stop. (a) Coding score; (b) total score (coding + start + RBS + upstream); (c) ORF GC minus the GC of the Prodigal model chosen for the contig; values outside each axis range are clipped to its edges. (d) Why the ORF was not called: no potential gene at that stop, negative coding score, positive coding score but start penalties make the total negative, or positive total but not chosen. Bacterial-hit candidates: best full-length target bacterial.

name: figL10_prodigal_lowscore
title: LOGAN: Prodigal genes the model scores low
caption: The second discordant class: complete Prodigal genes scoring below the 0.80-precision threshold. (c) Full-length structural hit rate of every length-matched arm (five databases), including the frameshift-shadow control.
